_README: The manifest that decides what news matters. YAAIN's filter reads THIS, not a hardcoded prompt. If you install something on brownie or the studio, or pin/upgrade a tool, UPDATE THIS FILE IN THE SAME BREATH — otherwise YAAIN decays into exactly the staleness it exists to prevent. Last audited against the machines: 2026-09-14 (refs/yaain-review-2026-09-14.md). Prior audit 2026-08-30 (refs/yaain-landscape-review-2026-08-30.md part (a)). AND WHEN YOU ADD A MODEL, WRITE ITS `chosen` BLOCK IN THE SAME COMMIT — the reason, the date, and a pointer to the entry that records it. A model with no recorded reason is one nobody can supersede on purpose later; if there genuinely was no decision, say so.

models.name: qwen3.8
models.detail: `bosun-brain` is **qwen3.8:27b-mlx** (Apple MLX build, nvfp4, 18.2GB on disk / ~19.4GB resident) at a PINNED num_ctx of 98,304 — without that pin Hermes auto-detects the training max. Also on the studio: qwen3.8:latest (Q4_K_M), and the qwen3.6 line (27b-bf16 / 27b-coding-bf16 / 27b-q8_0 / 27b-q4_K_M / 35b-a3b MoE) kept as rollback.
models.used_by: Bosun's own brain; repo-hunter enrich+explain; mac-hunter llm_generic; takomagether social drafts + council attribution

chosen.why: Em's call, taken in two steps on the same day. qwen3.8 over qwen3.6 on QUALITY: it beats 3.6 on all nine shared published benchmarks. Then MLX over GGUF on MEASURED SPEED, head to head at the same model and window — read 198.3/181.7/143.3 tok/s at 22K/45K/90K against GGUF's 179.2/164.0/139.9, and WROTE at 28.8 vs 15.7 tok/s, 83% faster. The 'MLX prefill collapses past 40K' claim that had justified a move back to GGUF is FALSE on this machine at every depth Bosun can reach. ⚠️ KNOWINGLY BOUGHT: nvfp4 has no published quality figures from anyone, for any model, where Q4_K_M does — a measured speed paid for with a quality assurance given up.
chosen.ref: observations.md 2026-09-12 (three entries); refs/studio-model-choice-2026-09-12.md; refs/exec-2026-09-13-bosun-brain-swap.md (EXECUTED — corrects its own handoff in four places); tracker bosun-brain-qwen38
chosen.revisit_if: a newer Qwen generation clears the same bars (Apache-2.0, ungated, ~27B class, served by Ollama), OR published quality figures appear for nvfp4 and contradict the bet. ⚠️ Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (180B) and Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B do NOT clear them — both are far beyond 128GB at any quantisation, and both carry an 'other' licence rather than Apache-2.0. Behaviour DID shift between formats: the MLX brain refused the watchdog's bare-token health check as injection-shaped where the GGUF brain complied. The probe was at fault and is fixed.

models.name: LTX-2.3
models.detail: LTX-2.3 22B dev + distilled Q4_K_M + a 7.6GB distilled LoRA. LOADS VIA UnetLoaderGGUF, not UNETLoader. RUN + MEASURED 2026-08-31: ~30s warm for a 4.84s clip at 768x512/25fps, peak VRAM 15,215 MiB of 16,303 — ~3x faster than Wan ti2v_5B. Text encoder is DualCLIPLoaderGGUF type=ltxv (gemma GGUF + embeddings connector); the LTX-native loaders are closed to us because they want a full safetensors checkpoint in checkpoints/. VIDEO ONLY IN PRACTICE — but see addons['⭐ CORRECTION']: the audio VAE is on disk and reachable through the ordinary VAELoader, so the path may be open and untried. Graph: hermes/workflows/ltx2.3-t2v-gguf.api.json

chosen.why: Installed as a second video path alongside Wan 2.2, notably for joint audio+video. RUN 2026-08-31 and it is the faster path for short clips (~3x Wan at comparable resolution), so it earns its place.

models.licence: TWO documents, and the one we cleared has MOVED. **LTX-2.3** was cleared 2026-08-31 against `LICENSE.md` — ⚠️ that path is now a 404 on GitHub, so the link in our notes and on the LTX-2.5-Diffusers model card is dead. The live document is `LICENSE-2_x` — the **LTX-2.x Community License Agreement, dated 2026-08-11**, which by its own §1.9 governs "all LTX-2.5 versions released since August 11, 2026, and all future releases of LTX-2.x". READ IN FULL 2026-09-14: **CLEAN for us.** Grant is non-exclusive, **worldwide**, non-transferable, royalty-free, for ANY purpose; **no territorial exclusion on use or on Output** (the sole 'territory' mention is OFAC/sanctions boilerplate, and the only EU/UK mention is a consumer-protection carve-out that PRESERVES rights); §5 Licensor claims **no rights in the Output**. Single gate: **$10,000,000 annual revenue** requires a paid licence. ⚠️⚠️ **THE ONE CLAUSE THAT CONSTRAINS US IS §6, AND IT IS NEW:** you may not remove, disable, alter or circumvent any **watermarking, content provenance, latent disclosure or metadata** applied to the Output — and if Lightricks believes you have, they **may revoke the licence immediately on notice**. Our media pipeline re-encodes through ffmpeg, which strips metadata by default, so ANY published LTX output must be checked for surviving provenance marks before it goes out. §6 also puts EU AI Act and California AI Transparency Act labelling duties on US as deployer. Attachment A: item 18 bars training a competing model; item 20 bars use in a product that directly competes with Lightricks' own — irrelevant to making our own clips, relevant only if we productised video generation.

addons.status: **FOUR INSTALLED ON BROWNIE 2026-09-14, all byte-verified against HF and all proven to load, apply and fit.** Em opened the gates on the three that matter the same day.
addons.what: 18 first-party LTX-2.3 add-ons on HF, 0.21-2.47GB each, ~14GB for all of them. Disk is not a constraint (1,345GB free on brownie).
addons.nodes_present: YES, verified live 2026-09-14 against brownie's ComfyUI (0.33.1, 1,423 nodes): LTXICLoRALoaderModelOnly, LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide(+Advanced), GetICLoRAParameters, ImagePrepForICLora. LTXICLoRALoaderModelOnly takes MODEL and returns MODEL, so it is type-compatible with UnetLoaderGGUF's output.
addons.⚠️ THE OPEN RISK: CLOSED 2026-09-14 — PROVEN, not assumed. `LTXICLoRALoaderModelOnly` was wired between `UnetLoaderGGUF` and `KSampler` in the committed t2v graph, everything else byte-identical including the seed. Both runs succeeded. **The outputs differ** (229,701 vs 256,957 bytes, different sha256), which is the proof that matters: a silently-ignored LoRA would have produced an identical file. Both clips are 4.84s / 768x512 / 25fps with no frozen segments.
addons.⚠️ THE SECOND RISK: MEASURED ACROSS ALL FOUR 2026-09-14, and the intuition was WRONG. Peak VRAM: control 15,194 · Foley 15,482 · upscaler 15,610 · In-Outpainting 15,642 · Motion-Track 15,706, all of 16,303. **An adapter costs ~300-500 MiB REGARDLESS of its file size** — the 1.31GB In-Outpainting peaked LOWER than the 0.33GB Motion-Track. The patch is applied per-layer and the peak is dominated by the base model and activations, not the adapter on disk. So do not size VRAM from a download size. ⚠️ Still true: ONE at a time. Two together would land near the ceiling; untested.
addons.the cheap test: DONE. Timings for the record: 75.3s cold (control, model load included), 33.0s warm (with the LoRA).
addons.which ones earn their keep: Mapped to real work rather than novelty: **In-Outpainting** (1.31GB) reframes 16:9 to 9:16, which is what Reels needs and what Walldog draws keep-clear zones for; **Pixel-Spatial-Upscaler** (1.31GB) — our clips render at 768x512, which is small; **Foley-V2A** (0.27GB) adds sound to video, and LTX-2.3 is VIDEO-ONLY for us today because the audio path needs a checkpoints/-only loader we do not have, so this may route around that limitation entirely. The rest (Water-Simulation, Instant-Shave, Cross-Eyed, Ingredients, HDR, Cinemagraph, DubIt, Cross-Eyed) are specific effects with no current use.
addons.⚠️ GATE — I GOT THIS WRONG TWICE, HERE I: **5 of 33 Lightricks LTX repos are unlocked on Em's account; 28 need a click.** The earlier '32 of 33 already accepted' was WRONG — it HEAD-requested whichever file came first, which for a gated repo is usually `README.md`, and **HF serves the model card publicly even when the weights are gated**. A second attempt was also wrong in the other direction, counting a 302 (the redirect to the signed CDN, i.e. success) as a refusal. THE RELIABLE TEST: range-request the first 1KB of the LARGEST .safetensors, following redirects, and require ~1024 bytes back. Sanity-anchor it on `Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, which is installed and running and must therefore read unlocked. UNLOCKED: LTX-2.3 · LTX-2.3-fp8 · LTX-2.3-nvfp4 · IC-LoRA-Motion-Track-Control · IC-LoRA-Union-Control. Everything else, including all of LTX-2.5 and the three add-ons worth having, is 403.
addons.licence: The LTX-2.3 add-ons carry the **LTX-2 Community License, 5 January 2026** — the one we cleared on 2026-08-31 — and it is EMBEDDED IN THE WEIGHTS' OWN METADATA, so that citation cannot 404 the way the GitHub link did. Verified in the installed file: non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, for any purpose; zero mentions of the EU, the UK or Korea. NB this is the JANUARY licence; LTX-2.5 carries the AUGUST LTX-2.x one instead.
addons.installed: models/loras/: ltx-2.3-22b-ic-lora-in-outpainting-0.9 (1,308,778,338 B) · ltx-2.3-22b-ic-lora-pixel-spatial-upscaler-x2-0.9 (654,465,286 B) · ltx-2.3-22b-lora-foley-v2a-1.0 (226,709,270 B) · ltx-2.3-22b-ic-lora-motion-track-control-ref0.5 (327,309,314 B, the proof run). ⚠️ The upscaler ships x2 AND x4; only x2 is installed — x4 is a second download.
addons.what is wired, and what is not: **Loading is proven for all four; NONE is wired to do its actual job yet** — each needs its own input path, and the load test deliberately reused the plain text-to-video graph to isolate the question 'does the adapter attach and fit'. **In-Outpainting / Upscaler:** every node needed is present (LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide + ImagePrepForICLora + GetICLoRAParameters); they need a source video and a guide path. Ordinary build work, no blockers found. Neither repo ships an example workflow — README only. **Foley is the hard one.** Its shipped `ltx-2.3-foley-v2a.json` cannot run here: it needs `ArbitraryCode` (x2) and `VideoSave_LTX`, **both ABSENT from our ComfyUI**, plus `CheckpointLoaderSimple` and `LTXVGemmaCLIPModelLoader`, which can only see `sd_xl_base_1.0` because we run GGUF and hold no LTX checkpoint. Rebuildable in principle — VideoSave_LTX maps to CreateVideo+SaveVideo which we already use, and the loaders map to our UnetLoaderGGUF + DualCLIPLoaderGGUF — but it is a build, not a rewiring.
addons.⭐ CORRECTION — the audio path may NOT be: Our note says LTX-2.3 is video-only for us because `LTXVAudioVAELoader` is one of the `checkpoints/`-only loaders. **That is true of THAT loader and appears NOT to close the path.** Checked 2026-09-14: `LTXVAudioVAEDecode` and `LTXVEmptyLatentAudio` both take a GENERIC `VAE` input, and the ordinary `VAELoader` already lists `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled_audio_vae.safetensors` — it is on disk in models/vae/ and reachable. So the route around is VAELoader -> LTXVAudioVAEDecode, bypassing LTXVAudioVAELoader entirely. UNTESTED — but the recorded blocker is not the blocker we thought, and that is worth an attempt before anyone concludes audio needs the 46GB checkpoint.

Installed behind a pip constraints file pinning torch/torchvision/numpy/transformers because controlnet_aux's requirements list unpinned torch -- the freeze diff was additions only, 0 changes, and LTX-2.3 re-ran clean as a regression check. constraints: VRAM <= 16GB on brownie. This is the single most important filter on relevance — most model announcements are written for 24-80GB cards. A quantisation that brings a model under 16GB is itself the news.

LICENCE IS A HARD SPEC, NOT A PREFERENCE. Apache-2.0 and MIT are the defaults. TERRITORIAL RESTRICTIONS ARE DISQUALIFYING - MiniMax H3 was deleted over exactly this (2026-08-29), and Hunyuan3D 2.0's territorial exclusion of the EU/UK/South Korea is still awaiting a ruling. A gated model costs a human licence click.
Blackwell sm_120 compatibility on brownie is real breakage, not a footnote.
brownie runs Python 3.13.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130. Wheels built for another torch do not load.
Off-API preference: local first, metered only where metering is the point.
Loader dependencies matter as much as models (LTX-2.3 loads through UnetLoaderGGUF, not UNETLoader).

licence_policy.disqualifying: any territorial restriction on use OR on the output; any non-commercial clause
licence_policy.needs_human: gated models (a licence click), and any bespoke community licence

_CHOSEN: Every model carries a dated `chosen` block: WHY we picked it, WHEN, a pointer to the dated entry that is the real record, and where known what would supersede it. The point is that when something newer appears we can weigh it against the reason rather than just mute it. Where no decision was ever recorded the block SAYS SO rather than inventing one. The `ref` is a pointer, never a restatement — the journal entry is the source of record.

retired.name: MiniMax H3
retired.why: DELETED, Em's call, on licence: the MiniMax H3 Community Licence carries territorial and commercial-use restrictions, which makes it unusable for a publication. 39.56GB reclaimed across four files; it had never been run, and LTX-2 also does joint audio+video, which was its distinguishing feature. Recorded because it is the strongest precedent we have for licence-as-a-hard-spec — and so a successor is not proposed without reading its licence first.
